# Returning Production

> **Two source classes on this page, never mixed in one claim.** *How the guide defines it*, *how the guide uses it* and every page reference are **GUIDE CONTENT**. *Working definition*, *why it matters* and any arithmetic over printed figures are **TTW DERIVED** — this library's words, supplied because the guide supplies none. ## How the guide defines it

p. 2: `RS – Returning Starters`.

## How the guide uses it

One of the guide's most heavily mechanised concepts. Makinen's Stability material on pp. 40–44 turns returning-starter counts into explicit transition systems with thresholds: nine or more returning offensive starters including the quarterback, thirteen or more starters overall, four or fewer offensive starters, at least eight fewer starters than the prior season. Those thresholds fire directly into win-total bets — 21 of the 29 bets on pp. 22–27 rest on them.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

How many of a team's starters from the previous season are back, counted overall and by side of the ball.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the guide's proxy for how much a team has to rebuild. Uniquely among the concepts here, it is not used as colour: it is used as a threshold that either trips a system or does not.

## How bettors use it in this guide

As a binary trigger. Houston's nineteen returning starters and Stability Score of 18 are cited as one of two such profiles nationally; Toledo's six players with starting experience are cited as the reason to bet the Under.

## Where it appears

pp. 40–44 for the systems; pp. 22–27 for them applied; every team page for the counts.

## Caution

Different contributors count returning production differently. On North Texas, one writes that zero starters return while another writes that eight percent of snaps do. Both are printed; neither is reconciled.
